# T0.17 — the repetition loop inside the benchmark's function, as TSVC has it (packaging v6): does a temporary array cost once again, and does anything else change?

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** pre-flight

## The question

The author, 4 Oct, on the clean layout (v5): "I do not like that this solution make the speed up worse … the tmp array is also a problem". In v5 the function is ONE repetition, called 48 times, so a temporary array obtained inside it is obtained on every call. Layout tested (v6, suite `tsvc_c2`): v5 with the repetition loop and TSVC's `dummy` call inside the function, where TSVC's own function has them. Per loop: identical output; the expert reference as fast as in the one-file packaging (v4) on the same lane, the reference with malloc/free inside the function included; DiscoPoP's view and the order statement as in v4; then sizes, classes and references through the harness.

## Result in one paragraph

Pre-flight (server and Mac, no model): the program is the same (output byte for byte, 44 of 44). Measured alike — one 12-core lane, variants interleaved — the expert references reach the same in the one-file packaging, in v5 and in v6 (median 3.27×, 3.19×, 3.32×); the 'lower ceiling' reported for v5 compared a lane with a whole node. The real cost of v5 is the temporary array: the five references that need one, written with malloc and free in the function, reach 0.39–1.09× in v5 and 1.36–2.60× in v6 (v4: 1.41–2.39×). DiscoPoP's view as in v4 on 40 of 42 loops (Mac, one draw; the two others differ in which blocker is named); the order statement right on 42 of 42, the repetition loop's request included.

| 2026-10-04 | plan | **T0.17 — the repetition loop back INSIDE the benchmark's function, as TSVC has it (packaging v6, suite `tsvc_c2`): a pre-flight, no model — registered before any of it runs through the harness; no model reads these files before the author has seen them and said so.** Why: the cost the author does not accept (row below) is the LAYOUT's. Packaging v5 made the function ONE repetition and let `main.c` call it 48 times, so whatever a solution obtains inside the function it obtains on every call. TSVC's own function holds its repetition loop and calls `dummy(a, b, c, d, e, aa, bb, cc, 0.)` between two repetitions (`benchmarks/TSVC_2/src/tsvc.c`; `dummy.c`: "called in each loop to make all computations appear required"), and so did E1-final's packages — where every arm that used a temporary array obtained it in front of the loop (the counts in the row below). v5 took the loop out because v4's version of it came with a note, with `pb_mix` and with protected lines; none of those is needed to have the loop. **The form (v6):** `<name>.c` — one `#include "data.h"` and the function: `for (int nl = 0; nl < iterations; nl++) {` TSVC's loop text `dummy(a, b, c, d, e); }` — no comment, no `pb_` name, the one editable file; `data.h` — v5's plus `#define iterations N` and the prototype of `dummy`; `main.c`, ours — `dummy` (the change of a few input values that `pb_mix` made, on its own arguments, counted by its own calls) and `main` with ONE call of the function between the timer's two calls; the measurement header outside the package as in v5. No note, no protected line: what keeps the repetitions honest is the output check (a repetition skipped, merged or run out of order changes the dump), as it catches any wrong program. **What comes back with the loop, stated:** a solution may do work once in front of the repetitions (the point), and may get the repetitions wrong (counted as a wrong program; the read-out of any experiment on v6 names how many unusable programs changed the repetition loop or the `dummy` call); the agent's first region is the repetition loop again, as in E1-final. `dummy` is TSVC's name and in TSVC it does nothing; here it changes input values, and a model can read that in `main.c`. **Pass criteria, no model:** (1) output byte for byte v4's on the shipped and the perturbed input, every loop; (2) speed, one lane, variants interleaved (a scratch tool, `preflight/tools/speed_probe.py`): the expert reference in v6 — its temporary array obtained with malloc in front of the loop and released after it — within noise of v4's; beside it v5's reference as committed (the array kept in a `static` pointer) and v5's reference written the ordinary way (malloc and free in the function); (3) DiscoPoP's view of the loop under study as in v4, two draws on the server (`t0_17_server_a`, `t0_17_server_b`); (4) the order statement under prompt version 4 right on every profile, the repetition loop's own request included (`order_replay.py --repetition-loop`); (5) then the sizes (`t0_1_c2_sizes`), the classes in three draws (`t0_11_c2_a`, `t0_11_c2_b`, `t0_11_c2_c`) and the references through the harness (`t0_14_c2_refs`). **Also measured, because it was named as a cost of v5:** the data declared as arrays, as TSVC declares them, instead of pointers the compiler cannot tell apart (variant `c2arr`, prototype only); whole-program optimisation (`-flto`). Whether anything of this is adopted, and what is run on it, is the author's decision | Plan, T0.17 |
